newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo stops Archbishop Monsengwo leaving country.
newsitem.headline: Congo stops Archbishop Monsengwo leaving country.

text.p: Roman Catholic Archbishop Laurent Monsengwo, who played a prominent political role in the former Zaire, on Saturday said he had been refused the right to leave Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of Congo.
Monsengwo said authorities at Ndjili airport seized his passport on Friday evening, preventing him from flying to Brazzaville in neighbouring Congo, from where he had a connecting flight to Brussels.

"I don't know why this happened. We are looking into it with the authorities," Monsengwo told Reuters. "They say they will return my passport to me today." He added that it was not clear when he would be allowed to leave.

Monsengwo, who is archbishop of the eastern city of Kisangani, was seen as a possible interim succesor to ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko days before Kabila's forces reached Kinshasa on May 17 after a seven-month bush war.
He was put forward by the transition parliament for the post of speaker from which he had been ousted in 1995.
Monsengwo, a respected mediator, defused numerous political crises in the early 1990s as chairman of a national conference shortly after Mobutu announced the return of multiparty democracy.
Since reaching Kinshasa the governing Alliance of Democratic Forces has banned political activity, dissolved the transition parliament and awarded Kabila sweeping powers under a presidential decree.
